questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

She __is being waited__ for you for two hours.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **has been waiting​​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The present perfect continuous is a verb tense that shows something which started in the past and is continuing at the present time.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + has/have been + V1 + -ing + since/for + object.
 
 
 
• Since is used for a point of time (1982, last month, etc.) whereas for is used for any duration (4 days, 6 months, etc.).
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He has been walking for two hours.*
 
 
 
• As a duration i.e. two hours has been given in the question, present perfect continuous tense i.e. has been waiting will be used.

 

Correct Sentence__: *She** has been waiting** for you for two hours. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The train was delayed __in order to __an accident.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **owing to​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​

__
 
• ​There are some fixed prepositional phrases given below:

 
 
• ​by the dint of, out of jealousy, in danger, by the dozen, owing to, on a trip, for a change, etc.
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• *​I went on a trip to Goa last month.*
 
 
 
• ​The phrase '**in order to**' means **with the aim or purpose of doing something.**
 
• The phrase '**owing to**' means** because of.**
 
• As per the context of the sentence, **the train got delayed due to an accident.**
 
• Thus the prepositional phrase '**owing to**' will be the correct choice.
 
• We can't use 'because and Since' because these words are conjunction and we know that after the conjunction we need to write a clause and which is not written in the sentence. 'an accident' is a phrase.

 

Correct Sentence__: *The train was delayed **owing to** an accident.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

Two elderly ladies narrated an rather improbable story to the police.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **narrated a rather​​**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• ​Articles are words that define a noun as specific or unspecific.
 
• The definite article 'the' is used with the name of things that are unique or already mentioned before.
 
• The article 'a' is used with the name of things that are not specific.
 
• The article 'an' is used with the words having the first letter as a vowel and having the sound of a vowel.
 
• In the part given in the **1st **option, the article 'a' will be used before the adverb 'rather' as '**rather**' doesn't start with a vowel.
 
• Also, we can write this sentence in two ways- Rather an improbable story and A rather improbable story.
 
• **When 'rather' acts as an adjective use 'a rather' and when 'rather' acts as an adverb use 'rather a' here in the given sentence 'improbable' is an adjective that is used to qualify a noun 'story' hence for the adjective we need an adverb to qualify it which is given i.e. 'rather' **

 

​Correct Sentence__:* **Two elderly ladies narrated **a rather** improbable story to the police. Or Two elderly ladies narrated **rather an improbable story **to the police.*​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
